meta.heading: Round 6: the next-gen prototype and the timesheet
meta.intro: Everything so far, put together as one working app you can click through: the time ribbon, the Desk, Planner, Canvas, Timesheet, and capture that understands plain sentences. All data is made up. Round 5 is in the Archive with my replies.

r6-proto.title: Open the prototype full screen and use it for five minutes
body: **[Open the Shiftbook prototype](https://claude.ai/artifact/74U1B2bff8opXBKdorjgLM)** in its own tab, full screen. It works with mouse and keyboard and keeps what you do until you reload.
bullets: Press **Ctrl+Space** and type `2h rack cleanup INC0045701 #data yesterday`. Watch it pick out the hours, project, ticket and day as you type, then press Enter and the entry flies into place.
On the Desk, hover an entry and press **+15m** (no more `=1.5+2`). Click a ticket chip to copy it. Every change has **Undo**; there are no "Are you sure?" boxes.
Click any day in the **ribbon** at the top to jump to it. The coloured bars are your hours by project.
**Planner**: drag the bottom edge of a block to stretch or shrink its hours. The ribbon and timesheet follow.
**Canvas**: drag a card out of Data centre into Patching and it changes project (with Undo). Right-click a card for the fold-out menu.
Keys **1–4** switch views. The **◐** button flips light and dark. The **Protected** pill starts the 10-minute screenshot allowance.

figures.caption: The same prototype, small, right here. The full-screen tab is much better.

r6-proto.pick: Yes. The fonts and colours ship inside the app (no internet), and the motion turns itself off if Windows is set to reduce motion.

r6-timesheet.title: What the timesheet looks like, and the quick way to fill it
body: Your Excel had no timesheet view at all, just "filter by Week Of". In Shiftbook the timesheet is a view of the week: **codes down the side, days across**, in the order you type them into your timesheet system. Hours fill in from what you logged; you never re-type them.
**Quick ways to add timesheet time when you don't want details:**
bullets: **Type straight into a cell.** Click under Wednesday on a code and type `2`. That's it: two hours of quick time on that code, no project or description needed.
**+ Holiday** books a day off at 8 h on your holiday code in one click.
From anywhere, **Ctrl+Space** then `8 holiday fri` does the same.
**Copy for timesheet** copies the grid as columns that paste straight into a timesheet form or Excel.
Amber warnings catch mistakes before you submit: hours with no code, weekdays with nothing logged, days over 12 h. **Mark submitted** stamps the week.

figures.caption: Click a code name to see the entries behind its hours. Click the amber **Unassigned** row, then the button, to give Admin a code.

options.why: Say what's missing, e.g. comments per day, a second code level.
They live only in your encrypted data, never in the repo or on this sheet.
A simple CSV you make yourself.

r6-timesheet.pick: Yes. Your real codes go into the app itself, so nothing about your workplace ends up in the code.

r6-excel.title: What your spreadsheet taught me
body: I studied how your workbook is built: its sheets, formulas and limits. I did not copy any of your entries into the repo or onto this sheet. Here's how each pain point is handled:

head: In Excel
In Shiftbook
rows: One ticket per cell, so you wrote "Multiple" or "NA"
Any number of ticket chips per entry; paste a list and they split. A Tickets page searches them all.
Worked on it again? Add a row or type `=1.5+2`
**+15m / +30m / +1h** on the entry, or stretch it in the Planner.
A script moves last week to an Archive sheet every Monday
Nothing to archive. Older days just fade back; everything stays searchable.
Dashboard of formula tiles; change a yellow week box
The ribbon shows every day's hours at a glance; click any day or week.
Daily routine items show OVERDUE forever
Routine items have alerts off and just collect hours.
Codes × days grid, quick-fill, warnings, copy.
Formulas break if a name is retyped differently
Projects are picked, not typed; renames update everywhere.

bullets: Your file can be imported at milestone M9: it currently holds 2 projects, 3 recurring items and a handful of entries. The import will keep your multi-ticket cells as a note to split, as planned.

r6-m1.title: M1 is done: your data is locked with your password
body: The real app now creates an encrypted vault on first run, shows a one-time recovery key, and asks for your password every time it opens. These screens are deliberately plain; they get the prototype's look once you approve it.

I checked the result the way an attacker would: the database file on disk is random-looking bytes, and an ordinary SQLite tool reports "file is not a database". The password takes about half a second to check, so guessing it is very slow.

figures.caption: The one-time recovery key (a throwaway test key). You must retype two groups before continuing.
The unlock screen after a wrong password: one plain message, with no hint about what was wrong.

bullets: **Done:** encrypted database, vault, recovery key, unlock, Lock now (Ctrl+L), lock after 15 min idle or after the computer sleeps, change password, and screenshot protection on by default. 154 tests pass.
**Security checklist:** every must-have item from the research is in, apart from noticing when you lock Windows without sleeping (Tauri can't detect it yet), which is written down as a known limit.

**One version note:** the database library bundles SQLCipher 4.10. Newer versions fix two low-risk issues in features Shiftbook doesn't use (full-text search, database export). I'll move up as soon as the database toolkit allows it.
**Not yet:** choosing where data is stored at first run, and saving the recovery key as a file. Both need the file-picker add-on, which comes with backups in M9.

questions.legend: After you unlock with the recovery key (forgot password), what next?

options.value: Ask for a new password straight away
options.why: Otherwise you'd need the long key every time.

questions.legend: A "Make a new recovery key" button (asks for your password)

options.why: If the app closes while the key is on screen, this is how you get a new one.

questions.legend: The Copy key button on the recovery screen

options.why: It warns, and empties the clipboard after 60 seconds. Some people store keys in a password manager.

questions.placeholder: Shown in a greeting. Default is "Me". Stays on your computer only.

r6-m1.pick: New password straight away, the new-key button soon, and keep Copy with its warning.
